lanes.label: PRE
lanes.blurb: Runs once. Builds the benchmark universe out of manually curated InterPro families plus SwissProt decoys, and records what every sequence in it actually is.

lanes.label: Outside the pipeline
lanes.blurb: The step this benchmark deliberately does not own. You run whichever tool you are evaluating, however you like, on the universe FASTA.

lanes.label: POST
lanes.blurb: Runs per samplesheet. Scores one or more tool runs against the curated originals and ranks them against each other.

stations.label: Resolve reference databases
stations.blurb: Stages the seven reference databases the sampling needs: the InterPro hierarchy and mapping, the four member databases (NCBIFAM, PANTHER, HAMAP, PFAM), and SwissProt.

io.out: hierarchy + mapping + member alignment dirs + SwissProt FASTA

points: Any *_db left null is downloaded from the matching *_latest_link. The link, not *_version, decides what gets fetched — *_version is recorded for provenance only.
Downloads are published under <outdir>/pre/databases. Point the matching *_db at that directory on the next run instead of refetching tens of GB.
The four member databases can be skipped individually with --skip_hamap / --skip_ncbifam / --skip_panther / --skip_pfam; at least one must remain enabled.
InterPro and SwissProt cannot be skipped: InterPro defines the curated families being sampled, SwissProt supplies the decoys.
PFAM is the one database that needs preprocessing — Pfam ships every family concatenated in a single Pfam-A.seed, which is split into one PFxxxxx.sto per family keyed on the #=GF AC accession.
Alignment format is detected by sniffing the file, not by extension: NCBIFAM ships both FASTA (.SEED for NFxxxxxx) and Stockholm (TIGRxxxxx).
stations.caveat: The remote *_latest_link URLs have never actually been fetched — the download modules are exercised end to end against local fixture archives only, and the HAMAP URL in particular looks wrong. The download modules also ship without a SHA-pinned container: use -profile conda, or supply the database paths yourself.

stations.label: Deduplicate the InterPro tree
stations.blurb: Parses ParentChildTreeFile.txt into a tree with each family reachable once, then extracts the set of InterPro accessions that survived.
points: InterPro is a DAG, not a tree: a family reachable down two branches would be sampled twice and then score as its own duplicate. Deduplicating first is what prevents that.
The deduplicated hierarchy is used twice — here, and again by the sampler, which walks the tree rather than a flat list.

stations.label: Find candidate families
stations.blurb: Joins the surviving InterPro IDs to their member-database families through interpro.xml.gz, and counts membership in each staged database.

io.in: valid InterPro IDs, interpro.xml.gz, member DB dirs
io.out: candidate metadata + per-database family membership counts

points: EXTRACT_DB_METADATA is a single parameterised module fanned out over however many databases survived --skip_*. Adding a database is a new channel element, not new code.
Membership counts are what --min_membership is later tested against, so they are computed from the actual staged alignments rather than from InterPro's own numbers.

stations.label: Keep only families that exist
stations.blurb: Drops candidates that do not resolve to a family present in the downloaded databases.
points: InterPro lists member families that a given database release may not actually ship. Without this filter the sampler would pick families whose sequences cannot be materialised.

stations.label: Sample the tree
stations.blurb: Picks the families that will make up the benchmark, walking the deduplicated hierarchy so the sample spreads across branches.
points: Sampling walks the tree, not the flat list, so the sample is not dominated by whichever branch happens to be largest.
--min_membership sets the smallest family worth benchmarking; --num_per_db sets how many families are taken from each member database.
--seed exists only to reproduce a specific PRE run. By default the family pool is intentionally random: a fresh pool per PRE run is the sampling design.
Comparability across tool runs does not come from seeding — it comes from every run scoring against the same universe, which universe.sha256 enforces.

stations.label: Materialise the sequences
stations.blurb: Pulls the member sequences of every sampled family out of the staged alignments, writes one FASTA per family, and records identity for each sequence.
points: This is where the id_registry.tsv is born, and it is the whole reason the benchmark works. Protein-family tools do not round-trip sequence IDs: mgnifams emits 1814953751/178-297, proteinfamilies emits 2632373804_177_299/1-122, the curated original is keyed Q9X1J3/1-250.
Identity is therefore recorded at construction time rather than guessed downstream from the shape of whatever ID a tool wrote.
The module is told which database each staged directory is, because staging renames directories to break basename collisions between user-supplied paths.

stations.label: Spike in decoys
stations.blurb: Adds negative controls: SwissProt proteins that align to none of the curated families, so a tool that over-recruits can be caught doing it.
points: DIAMOND is run rather than sampling SwissProt blindly: every SwissProt protein is searched against the curated set, and only the ones with no hit are eligible as decoys.
The registry is extended with the decoy rows here, so source_type is recorded by PRE instead of being inferred from an ID shape by POST.
universe.sha256 is written at the same moment as the FASTA, which is what lets POST later refuse a mismatched pairing.

stations.label: The universe
stations.blurb: The three files that define one benchmark experiment, plus the curated originals POST scores against. Keep them together.
points: pre/combined_decoy.faa — feed this to the family-generation tool.
pre/families/sampled/id_registry.tsv — the identity ledger every POST metric resolves through.
pre/universe.sha256 — the checksum that ties a tool run to the universe it was produced from.
pre/families/sampled/sampled_fasta/ — the curated originals.
pre/families/sampled/updated_sampled_metadata.csv — which family came from which database layer.
pre/databases/ — whatever was downloaded, kept for reuse.
stations.caveat: A v1.0.0 universe cannot be scored by v2.0.0: id_registry.tsv and universe.sha256 did not exist before v2.0.0, so PRE must be rerun.

stations.label: Your family-generation tool
stations.blurb: Whatever tool you are evaluating — nf-core/proteinfamilies, mgnifams, or something of your own — run on combined_decoy.faa, on your own terms.

io.out: a full-family MSA directory (+ an optional clustering TSV)

points: PRE and POST are two separate runs, not two halves of one DAG, precisely because this step sits between them. Wiring them together would mean owning the tool invocation, which a tool-agnostic benchmark cannot do.
The MSA directory must be the FULL-FAMILY MSA directory, not a seed MSA. A seed MSA is not full family membership, and pointing at one measures something different.
Supplying the optional clustering TSV switches on the clustering investigation, whose cluster-ID cross-check is what detects exactly that seed-MSA misconfiguration.
Example: nextflow run proteinfamilies --input samplesheet.csv --clustering_tool cluster --cluster_size_threshold 3 --cluster_seq_identity 0.5 --save_non_redundant_fams_fasta true
stations.caveat: A tool that fully renames its sequences (hash IDs, integer reindexing) cannot be resolved against the registry. unmapped_fraction goes to 1.0 and the run fails loudly, by design; such a tool needs a per-tool mapping file.

stations.label: Validate the samplesheet
stations.blurb: Reads one row per tool run and turns it into a meta map, so everything downstream fans out per run and publishes under its own directory.
points: Columns: sample, tool, msa_dir, clustering_tsv.
msa_dir is required and must be the full-family MSA directory.
clustering_tsv is optional. When present, POST runs the clustering investigation and cross-checks cluster IDs; when absent, that process is simply skipped.
Several runs in one samplesheet is the normal case — that is what makes the final report a cross-run ranking rather than a single score.

stations.label: Resolve identity
stations.blurb: Resolves every ID the tool emitted through the PRE registry and splits the tool's sequences into curated originals, decoys and unknowns.

io.out: per-run sequence stats and the original count

points: Every metric downstream is a set intersection on universe_id strings resolved here — never on the raw text of a tool's IDs.

The universe checksum is verified at this point. POST refuses to score a samplesheet against a universe it was not built from: pointed at tool outputs made from different input, it fails with a high unmapped_fraction rather than silently reporting zeros.
parent_id coverage is reported as auxiliary QC only and is not part of the ranking.
The original counts feed the coverage denominator, which is why this runs before coverage.
stations.caveat: Always check post/<sample>/reproducibility_stats/jaccard_qc.tsv first. If unmapped_fraction is not ≈ 0, the IDs did not resolve and no downstream number means anything.

stations.label: Decoy recruitment
stations.blurb: Counts how many of the SwissProt decoys the tool pulled into its families.
points: Decoys have no curated family by construction, so anything recruited from them is an unambiguous false positive.
1 − decoy_recruitment_rate is one of the five scorecard components.

stations.label: Pair families up
stations.blurb: Computes Jaccard similarity between each generated family and each curated original, and emits the edgelist the report is built on.
points: Jaccard is symmetric and one-to-one: it says how well families pair up, but it cannot tell a tool that split one family into five from one that merged five into one. That is why P/R/F1 and split/merge topology are computed separately.
--match_threshold (default 0.5) is the bar for calling a pair a reported family match.
Do not conflate --match_threshold with --association_threshold (default 0.1): they are two different notions of "match" living in one report.

stations.label: Per-family P / R / F1
stations.blurb: One row for every generated/original pair whose universe_id intersection is non-empty.
points: precision_denom = |G| (the generated family), recall_denom = |O| (the curated original).
f1 is their harmonic mean; jaccard_denom = |G ∪ O|.
mean_f1 across pairs is the headline component of the scorecard.

stations.label: Split / merge topology
stations.blurb: Detects the failure modes Jaccard is blind to: one curated family shattered across many generated ones, or many collapsed into one.
points: Counts are directional and computed within each db_layer: split associations use precision(G,O), merge associations use recall(G,O).
Both require |G ∩ O| ≥ --min_intersection_size (default 3), so a single shared sequence does not create an edge.
--association_threshold (default 0.1) decides which edges are considered for topology at all. It is a heuristic.
1 − split_merge_rate is a scorecard component.

stations.label: Coverage
stations.blurb: How much of the curated universe the tool reconstructed at all — by sequence, and by family, per database layer.
points: A tool can score a high mean F1 on the families it did produce while covering only a fraction of the universe. Coverage is what keeps that honest.
Both family_coverage and sequence_coverage are scorecard components.
Reported per db_layer (NCBIFAM / PANTHER / HAMAP / PFAM), so a tool that is strong on one curation style and weak on another is visible.

stations.label: Per-run scorecard
stations.blurb: Folds the five components into one composite per tool run.

io.in: family metrics + split/merge summary + coverage + decoy stats

points: The five components are mean_f1, family_coverage, sequence_coverage, 1 − decoy_recruitment_rate and 1 − split_merge_rate, all keyed on universe_id.
It consumes the family metrics and the split/merge summary, joined back onto the sample they came from rather than relying on channel order.
--scorecard_weights re-weights the composite. Every raw component is published beside it, so you can re-weight after the fact.
stations.caveat: The composite ships labelled EXPLORATORY. Equal weights are arbitrary-but-defensible and association_threshold = 0.1 is a heuristic. Do not present it as settled.

stations.label: Rank the runs and report
stations.blurb: The deliverable: one row per tool run, ranked, with every raw component published beside it so the ranking is auditable.

io.in: every run's scorecard, metrics, summary and coverage

points: COMPARE_BENCHMARK_RUNS is the only step that sees every run at once — a .collect() is what makes it cross-run. Everything before it is per-sample.
Ranked by the EXPLORATORY composite, rank 1 = highest, sorted descending.
The stacked barplots, db family coverage and size distributions are still per-sample; they all read the Jaccard edgelist.
--skip_multiqc turns off the rendered report without touching the CSVs.
stations.caveat: The end-to-end benchmark against real curated InterPro families has not been run yet.

gotchas.title: Identity comes from the registry, never from the ID text
gotchas.body: Protein-family tools do not round-trip sequence IDs. PRE records identity at construction time in id_registry.tsv and POST resolves every observed ID through it. Any metric you see is a set intersection on universe_id, not on the string a tool happened to write.

gotchas.title: The three PRE files travel together
gotchas.body: combined_decoy.faa, id_registry.tsv and universe.sha256 define one experiment. POST verifies the checksum and refuses to score a samplesheet against a universe it was not built from.

gotchas.title: Read jaccard_qc.tsv before anything else
gotchas.body: If unmapped_fraction is not ≈ 0, the IDs did not resolve and no downstream number means anything — including a healthy-looking rank.

gotchas.title: Two thresholds, two meanings
gotchas.body: match_threshold (0.5) is a reported family match. association_threshold (0.1) is an edge considered for split/merge topology. They coexist in one report and must never be conflated.

gotchas.title: Full-family MSAs, not seed MSAs
gotchas.body: A seed MSA is not full family membership. Pointing msa_dir at one silently measures something different — supply the optional clustering_tsv and the cluster-ID cross-check will catch it.

gotchas.title: The ranking is EXPLORATORY
gotchas.body: Equal component weights are arbitrary-but-defensible and the association threshold is a heuristic. Every raw component is published so you can re-weight; do not present the headline ranking as settled.

gotchas.title: Seeding is not what makes runs comparable
gotchas.body: By default the family pool is intentionally random — a fresh pool per PRE run is the sampling design. Comparability comes from every tool run scoring against the same universe, which universe.sha256 enforces. Use --seed only to reproduce one specific PRE run.
